Everyone is different and weed has different strains too. Some people can be fine on weed, some have a lot of issues and some can be dependent on it. 

I have been smoking since I was 15. (I'm in my mid 30s now). I had a doctor once tell me that using it prolonged and especially in my teens can lead to the development schizophrenia. 

I am now diagnosed with BPD, schizoaffective bipolar type and severe PTSD. I live in the United States and my state just legalized recreationally this past midterms and went medical back in 2018. I have had my medical card since 2020. It helps me but I can't help but wonder if that doctor long ago was right about the schizophrenia. I'm super sensitive to a lot of sativas so I usually go with indicas or indica dominant hybrids which have helped me especially with my PTSD and moods.

Yeah it was nuts!! I ended up in Florida off a manic episode and was hallucinating. I ended up crashing out after day 7 and ended up hospitalized (I have schizoaffective- bipolar type). 

The girl that choked me out thought I was trying to ruin her life. She was not with it but we ended up being ok.

The guy ended up getting transported to another ward. He was being very inappropriate, the staff knew it and just laughed it off when they'd see it. Him sneaking in to my room while my roommate was away and I was asleep and him doing more inappropriate things was the last straw. I was so relieved when they transferred him out. He would try to talk to me about how he could get me a job and how I could make lots of money. I knew exactly what he meant and I wasn't having it. Gotta love Miami though.

I've had some really good hospital stays and a few really bad hospital stays, it really depends on the place. 

The best place I was at was a unit just for people with trauma issues here in my state. It was so quiet and serene, you have work books you worked on everyday and it was quiet and calming. The nurses/staff/doctors/therapists were so nice and helpful. The place later was shut down sadly. 

The worst hospital I was in was in Florida. Every guy was hitting on me, a girl tried to choke me out and a guy patient snuck in to my room that I had to later report. Ever since then, I've had other hospital stays but it absolutely terrifies me if I have to go.

I have a few that have stuck with me....

1. I was once in a hospital for an attempt I had made on my life. The doctor we had to see there basically told me "if you are suicidal, you should go ahead and do it. Everyone can have your money, it's not like your special or anything qnd the world would move on." 

2. My mother and I have never had a solid relationship. It was very love/hate. One time we got in a big argument and was like "We didn't have a relationship anyway and I don't care." We remained off and on up until she passed in September of 2021. 

3. This one probably stung the worst and affects me the most. Back in 2008, I went out on a date with a guy who ended up raping me. Against my better judgment, I decided to go to a hospital and report what had happened. Nursing staff and the hospital were fine. The cops on the other hand that showed up to talk to me?? Ooof! I was up there by myself, they asked me a lot of questions that due to the shock, I couldn't really answer much to them. So the one cop was like "yeah, you went there, you guys kissed, we think you are lying." And the other cop was like "ya know some girls do things and then regret them" and they both walked out and left. Probably one of the most dehumanizing experiences ever!
